issue_context.title: GROUP_CONCAT(float) is not compatible with mysql
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)
```mysql
CREATE TABLE `t2`  (
  `col1` float GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((`col102` + 10)) STORED NOT NULL,
  `col102` float,
  PRIMARY KEY (`col1`) USING BTREE
)

INSERT INTO `t2` VALUES (DEFAULT, 3.36769e38);
INSERT INTO `t2` VALUES (DEFAULT, 3.18374e38);
```
<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
```mysql
mysql> select  GROUP_CONCAT(col1)  from t2;
+-----------------------+
| GROUP_CONCAT(col1)    |
+-----------------------+
| 3.18374e38,3.36769e38 |
+-----------------------+
1 row in set (0.03 sec)

```
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
```mysql
mysql> select  GROUP_CONCAT(col1)  from t2;
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GROUP_CONCAT(col1)                                                              |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 318374000000000000000000000000000000000,336769000000000000000000000000000000000 |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.06 sec)
```
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)
```mysql
Community
Git Commit Hash: 058e52ad7c1b477147dcb933b3f1b3b2be31e998
Git Branch: heads/refs/tags/v4.0.11

```

comments:
@Howie59 @wanliyi @guo-shaoge @djshow832 I'm curious is this a significant concern of compatibility? Results are the same and only representation different.

@Howie59 according to this comment ( https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/23964#discussion_r651591316 ), do you investigate how MySQL handles casting from float to string? It seems the behavior depends on context which make the issue complex.

review_comments:
Looks like this change may cause compatible issues.

    drop table if exists t;
    create table t(c1 float(16, 4));
    insert into t1 values(3.1415926535);

Before change, compatible:

    mysql> select concat('a', c1) from t1;
    +-----------------+
    | concat('a', c1) |
    +-----------------+
    | a3.1416         |
    +-----------------+
    1 row in set (0.00 sec)

After changed, not compatible.

    mysql> select concat('a', c1) from t1;
    +-----------------+
    | concat('a', c1) |
    +-----------------+
    | a3.1416e+00     |
    +-----------------+
